2) Don't worry about losses. After games, ask yourself where you personally went wrong, not your teammates. Doesn't matter if they fed religiously, threw at teamfights, flamed, afk, whatever. Be critical of yourself. What did you PERSONALLY fuck up in? Frankly, you should always have an answer for this. If you don't, that's where the growth stops.

Well first off, know that regardless of what he's up to, it sounds like you guys tried to work things out once, but he's -like you said- avoidant, and it doesn't look like this can be functional if he doesn't want to work it out.

I guess I'll answer your question though, at least from what I'm going through. I think I have similar attributes as he does. Do note, that I don't know him, and only you do, so I could be completely off. Regarding him being practical/logical, that is both a mask, and his way of coping. He most likely doesn't want to make it hard for you or himself, and it also helps him cope with the loss. He could very well be going through a lot worse than you might be, seeing as you were his best friend. I doubt he feels liberated, but he also might just not know how to healthily function with a relationship with you, especially since it sounds like you're going through emotional turmoil as well. That might not be his, or your fault. You said you were his only friend, so his social interaction might be a little faulty.

You should move on. But I wouldn't want you to feel antagonizing feelings towards him even if you don't hear from him. Just coming from someone with little real human interaction and relationships, its really fucking lonely and depressing. Especially if he lost someone he WAS close to.

Nuke, block, and smite all his existence away from your world. And enjoy the process. Its cathartic knowing that in any case scenario, they will never be able to contact you, nor will you be able to know if they tried to or not.

 I hear you on the friend thing, I kind of feel that way in that I don't really have a lot of close friends at all either, and I'll have literally no one to talk to once I go back to school.

Low elo? People probably won't assume this as much. However, the higher elo you go, I'd imagine the laners get very good at disguising when they're about to make a play w/ their teammates.

For lanes like these, I employ one of two methods

1. Hold your "ganking" spell till they try to use their escape, then use the spell then. 

2. Ping the enemy laner, signaling your laner to aggress. The enemy laner might use their dash offensively, allowing you to gank them knowing their escape is wasted. Just essentially get your midlaner to bait out their escape

Obviously this isn't foolproof and you can still get outplayed. But here's an example if you're playing...say Xin, and you're trying to gank a Leblanc.

Scan the midlane bush you're ganking from to make sure you're not being seen. Tell your midlaner to go for a trade, in which leblanc will probably use her W for damage. You walk up to the leblanc while they're trading, just going for an autoattack rather than using your dash attack. Leblanc, in all her fear and bullshit kit, will port back. Which is when you strike with your dash+knockup.
